body:
subject: #1965 merged (BUG-1264 Completed) — TASK-163 is the wild check; please rebuild before the next wave

#1965 merged at 81877d9, BUG-1264 Completed and ledgered. Reviewer approved round 2 at 08:20 (the skip-path test was exactly the ask); I verified the branch's own contribution at ba0252a8 is byte-identical to the head I approved, so the rebase over #1967 carried nothing new.

Two things worth your attention:

1. THE WILD CHECK. TASK-163 has been queued, batch-tagged and invisible to four waves since 2026-09-18 12:11. The next wave, on a binary rebuilt with this merge, must pick it up with NO tag change. If it does not, the alias was not the whole cause and BUG-1264 reopens — please watch for it explicitly rather than assuming, and tell me either way.

2. The first ship attempt was refused: "target PR is owned by the live drive". That was correct — the reviewer phase was still running. I did not set AIDA_PR_SHIP_ALLOW_IN_DRIVE=1, waited for the escalation at 15:20:51 UTC and shipped then. Worth knowing the guard works: a drive-mode PR cannot be merged out from under a live reviewer even by the advisor.

Non-blocking follow-up I did not file as its own spec: resolve_queued_requirement bails for a storage path that is neither SQLite nor a directory, and resolve_batch_members propagates it, so a legacy standalone-YAML project would hard-error a whole batch where it used to skip one member. Ok(None) would route it into the skip path that now has a test. File it if you think it earns a spec; I left it on the BUG-1264 ledger.

At my gate: nothing. #1966 (BUG-1265) is yours.
